chunks: Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad narrated from al-Barqī, from al-Nawfalī, from al-Sakūnī, from Jaʿfar, from his father, from ʿAlī عليه السلام, who said:

The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم said: “Do not ask the immoral woman who committed immorality with you, for just as immorality is insignificant to her, it is also insignificant to her to accuse the innocent Muslim.”

key_terms.الْبَرِيءَ: the innocent one, free of the accusation
key_terms.الْفَاجِرَةَ: the immoral woman; one openly characterized by grave indecency
key_terms.الْمُسْلِمَ: the Muslim whose honor and innocence are to be protected
key_terms.تَرْمِيَ: to accuse or cast an allegation against
key_terms.فَجَرَ: committed immorality or illicit sexual misconduct

ai.seo_question: Why should one not rely on the accusation of an openly immoral person against an innocent Muslim?
ai.summary: This hadith warns against relying on the word of a flagrantly immoral person in matters involving grave accusations. It highlights that one who treats sin lightly may also treat slander lightly, thereby endangering the honor of an innocent Muslim.
